item.description: DigitalCommons@UTEP (The University of Texas at El Paso) — As data increasingly shapes participation in society, there is growing emphasis on preparing youth to engage with data through computer science education. Existing K-12 computing and data science curricula have expanded opportunities for learners to analyze and interpret data; however, many learning experiences continue to rely on datasets and inquiry structures designed by others, limiting authentic engagement, personal relevance, and learner agency. item.description: Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University) — Spatial ability-the ability to understand, visualize, and mentally manipulate shapes and objects-is important for learning in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). item.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Geographic Information Systems for Environmental Monitoring and Climate-Resilient Urban Planning
item.description: Asian Journal of Advanced Research and Reports — Urban climate risks are produced through interactions between changing hazards, built form, ecological conditions, infrastructure and unequal social vulnerability. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), geographic information systems (GIS) and Earth observation now allow these interactions to be represented at increasingly fine spatial and temporal scales. Yet improved environmental maps do not necessarily constitute reliable predictions of human exposure, defensible estimates of intervention benefits or evidence of greater urban resilience. item.title: Temporal Evacuation Estimates: Insights and Mitigation Strategies for Wildfire Evacuations
item.description: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta) — During wildfire evacuations, timely action is essential to ensure life safety and minimize risk. As climate change increases the frequency and severity of wildfires, evacuation studies become necessary to improve emergency planning and ensure community resilience. However, temporal insights are not well-defined for wildfire evacuations due to data scarcity, resulting in a lack of time-based knowledge, especially for community-wide movement patterns. item.title: Global probabilistic forecasting of air pollution at the kilometre scale
item.description: Research Square — Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) refers to particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 µm or less. It comes from human activities, such as traffic and industry, and from wildfires, desert dust and gases emitted by vegetation. Short-term exposure to it accounts for about a million deaths a year. Operational forecasts run on grids tens of kilometres wide, which hide the pollution breathed by nearly two hundred million people a day. item.title: Strategic Resilience in Rail Infrastructure: Lessons from International Resilience Initiatives
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Climate change is escalating extreme weather, profoundly challenging global railways. UIC’s RERA (Resilient Railways) initiative addresses these threats through two reports: “Resilient Railways facing High Temperatures” and “Resilient Railways facing Heavy Rains”. While high temperatures can cause track buckling and heavy rainfall can lead to landslides, both disrupt services and compromise safety. item.title: Dynamic Accessibility and Resilience Assessment of Urban Transport Networks Under Flooding
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Flooding poses a major threat to urban transport networks, disrupting connectivity and access to essential services such as hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies. Assessing resilience is complicated by the differential exposure of roads to flood hazards and variable repair times. This study develops a dynamic accessibility and resilience framework to evaluate how floods affect access to critical services and how networks recover over time. item.title: Adaptive Centrality Measures and a Pareto-Based Approach for Transport Network Vulnerability Assessment: A Case Study of Thessaloniki
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract As cities face escalating disruptions from extreme weather and other urban hazards, strengthening transport network resilience is becoming an increasing priority. Network centrality measures are widely used to identify infrastructure components requiring priority investment; however, conventional purely topological applications often overlook traffic dynamics, which can lead to misleading results. item.title: Modeling and Quantifying Resilience in Multimodal Urban Transport Networks Under Flood Risks
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Urban transport systems function as intricate interdependent networks encompassing road, rail, and public transit modes. Given the increasing frequency of climate-induced disruptions, particularly urban flooding, there is an urgent imperative to model and quantify the resilience of multimodal systems under stress. While extant studies have addressed resilience within individual transport modes, few have examined the integrated behavior of multimodal systems during such disruptions, and even fewer have coupled topological network metrics with dynamic performance-based evaluations. item.title: Assessment of Flood Impact on Emergency Accessibility in Istanbul’s Road Network
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Floods are significant climate-induced natural disasters that frequently impact the resilience of urban areas, largely due to unplanned urbanization and increasing population density, which lead to inadequate infrastructure. This study evaluates the accessibility of emergency response services to flood-prone areas in Istanbul under 50-, 100-, and 500-year flood scenarios and assesses the vulnerability of the road network using Geographical Information Systems and machine learning techniques. item.title: AGORA cities: The hidden infrastructure shaping urban fragility
item.description: Environment and Planning B Urban Analytics and City Science — Urban services are unevenly distributed across the city, yet it is unclear when their joint presence signals fragility and when it instead outlines a neighbourhood’s vocation. For Bologna and Florence, we integrate Foursquare and OpenStreetMap points of interest with Sentinel-2-derived green indicators based on the 3–30–300 rule, cluster urban areas accordingly, and benchmark the clusters against the demographic, social, economic, and composite fragility indices produced by the municipal statistical offices, which are exogenous to the analysis. item.title: Navigating a Resilient Transition: A Conceptual Framework for Mapping Disruptions to Electrified Public Bus Transport
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Public transport plays a key role in decarbonizing the transport sector, but in Sweden, the sector is challenged by a slow post-Covid recovery. While vehicle electrification can offer new, cross-sectoral resilience services, it may also place additional strain on the sector through new infrastructure dependencies and potentially undermine the sector’s long-term resilience. This paper explores how resilience can be conceptualized in electrified public bus transport in Sweden, maps related disruptions and identifies the most critical resilience challenges perceived by stakeholders. item.title: Global overview on vehicular emission control: current strategies, effectiveness, challenges, and future research priorities
item.description: Clean Technologies and Environmental Policy — Controlling vehicle emissions remains a critical challenge for improving urban air quality. Although multiple emission control strategies have been adopted worldwide, their main characteristics and outcomes remain scattered, hindering a systemic understanding of what works, where, and under which conditions. This structured narrative review combines a structured literature search with an original regulatory maturity matrix, which scores programs to control vehicle emissions in 18 countries and regions and groups them by cluster analysis. item.title: Cargo Bikes as a Resilient Transport Mode in Emergency Scenarios
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract In crises such as power outages, natural disasters, or security-related disruptions, mobility systems must function under decentralized and resource-constrained conditions. Cargo bikes offer a promising yet underexplored contribution to resilience. They require no fuel or license, involve relatively low costs, and can be operated without specialized training, which makes them accessible to both emergency services and communities. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Railway assets such as bridges are important for the transport sector. Although railway bridge infrastructure across Europe has been operating for decades. The operation and maintenance of bridges are dependent on available data from official records and Internet of Things (IoT). Thus, as part of the EU-RAIL FP1 MOTIONAL project a prototype is implemented in Python programming based on Building Information Modeling (BIM) in Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) by seamlessly extracting data collected by IoT sensors for bridge operation. item.title: Designing Climate Resilience: A Policy Lab Approach to Climate Adaptation in Swedish Transport Systems
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Climate change increasingly challenges transport infrastructure, demanding adaptive governance across administrative levels. This project examines a design-driven policy lab involving four Swedish municipalities, a regional municipal association, and a reference group representing local, regional, and national authorities. Through facilitated exercises and tailored manuals, local officials identified barriers, mapped stakeholders, and jointly developed actionable adaptation strategies. item.title: Operational Resilience of Road Systems When Disruptions Arise
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Climate change driven hazards, including intense rainfall, flooding, and heatwaves, increasingly threaten road transport, disrupting mobility. As infrastructure age faster than they can be upgraded, the inability to respond swiftly to emerging threats results in cascading risks across the interdependent services like emergency response and healthcare. item.title: Resilient Urban Logistics for Disaster Response: Evaluating the Valencia Living Lab in the DISCO Project
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract The València Living Lab was established in response to the flash floods of 29 October 2024, which caused 230 fatalities and severe disruption across key municipalities in the province of València. Developed under the EU-funded DISCO project, the Living Lab aimed to test a scalable, sustainable logistics model for crisis response through a combination of infrastructure reuse, digital coordination, and green last-mile distribution. item.title: Simulation Framework to Evaluate Link Criticality in Multimodal Freight Transport Networks Using Operational Metrics
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Growing geopolitical risks and climate extremes have renewed interest in strengthening the resilience of transport networks to safeguard economic competitiveness and stability. A key step in network resilience planning is identifying critical components. While link criticality has been widely studied, freight networks present challenges due to their multimodal, multi-commodity nature. item.title: Contribution of Cross-Analysis of Crowdsourcing Geospatial Data, Photographic Data, and Satellite Image to a Road Maintenance Strategy
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract In low-income countries such as Madagascar, road infrastructure management is hindered by the absence of comprehensive databases and limited access to modern monitoring tools. This study addresses this challenge by assessing the quality of a main road network at the scale of a rural municipality in order to ensure territorial accessibility. The approach combines participatory science, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and Remote Sensing to identify both the extent and condition of the road network. item.title: Health impacts of water risks through water-borne and vector-borne diseases in informal settlements in the Global South and India
item.description: Discover Public Health — Abstract Informal settlements concentrate overlapping water risks that undermine health, well-being and livelihood security. This review synthesizes evidence on how water scarcity, poor water quality, flooding, infrastructure deficits and governance gaps interact to shape health outcomes in informal urban communities, with particular attention to water- and vector-borne diseases. item.description: Frontiers in Public Health — Background The joint effects of meteorological conditions and air pollutants on the risk of hospitalization for diabetes remain insufficiently understood, particularly due to the limited availability of large-scale time-series studies in northern China. Methods Daily hospitalization records of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in Urumqi City from January 1, 2019, to December 31, 2025, were collected, along with corresponding daily air pollutant concentrations and meteorological data. item.title: Mobile signaling data reveal spatial synchrony between mega event population hotspots and commercial zones across transit isochrones
item.description: Scientific Reports — Abstract Mega events cause late-night transit bottlenecks, yet point-based transit data cannot show where attendees are before entering stations. We quantified the spatial synchrony between mega-event population hotspots and nighttime commercial zones with mobile signaling data from the Busan Fireworks Festival. item.title: Heterogeneity in the global burden of non-communicable diseases attributable to low physical activity: spatial patterns, temporal trends, and population groups
item.description: International Journal of Health Geographics — Low levels of physical activity (LPA) remain an important and unevenly distributed global public health problem, contributing substantially to the burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs). However, the burden attributable to LPA varies considerably across geographic regions and population groups and has changed over time. This study aimed to characterize the temporal trends, population differences, spatial clustering, and geographic variation in the burden of NCDs attributable to LPA at the global, regional, and national levels. item.title: Food co-purchasing networks encode geographic disparities in cardiometabolic health
item.description: Research Square — Abstract Unhealthy diets are a major driver of cardiometabolic disease, yet the geospatial structure of dietary behavior and its links to population health remain poorly understood. While large-scale retail transaction data offer a unique view of population dietary behavior, conventional approaches reduce purchases to isolated items, not accounting for how foods are actually combined. item.description: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence — The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into social simulation has generated considerable enthusiasm, but also raises substantial methodological and epistemological challenges. This critical review examines the use of LLMs as cognitive or decision-making components of simulated agents from a computational social science perspective. item.title: Climate-related dysphoria: a proposed research agenda
item.description: Frontiers in Psychiatry — Climate change threatens mental health, but its contribution to everyday changes in mood remains difficult to distinguish from seasonal routines and other stressors. I propose climate-related dysphoria (CRD) as a provisional dimensional framework for affective worsening during adverse environmental exposure and improvement as exposure diminishes. item.description: Environmental Monitoring and Assessment — Abstract Glyphosate-based herbicides are widely used in commercial forest plantations to suppress competing vegetation, yet concerns persist regarding their persistence in soil, environmental contamination, and potential risks to human health. This study assessed the spatial distribution, seasonal variation, and associated human health risk of glyphosate and its main metabolite, aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA), in soils adjacent to water bodies in the Thathe Vondo Forest Plantation, Limpopo Province, South Africa. item.description: Scientific Reports — Abstract One of the biggest challenges in wastewater restoration is the creation of effective, stable, and environmentally safe photocatalysts for the breakdown of persistent organic pollutants. In order to increase the photocatalytic activity of amorphous silica, a series of silica@ graphene nanocomposites with varying graphene loadings (0.001–2 g) were successfully created using a simple sol–gel technique. item.title: Field testing of floating mat systems for grass cultivation and biochar generation under variable weather conditions
item.description: Environmental Sciences Europe — Variable weather conditions can substantially affect the stability and performance of a floating treatment wetland used to cultivate aquatic plants. This study evaluates the field performance and ecological potential of a floating foam mat designed to support aquatic plant growth and provide multiple benefits, including accumulation of nitrogen and phosphorus in plant biomass, atmospheric carbon sequestration, heavy metal removal, and biochar production. item.title: Asymmetric and dynamic effects of climate variability on crop and livestock production in Somalia
item.description: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems — Climate variability poses escalating risks to agricultural systems in fragile and climate-exposed regions, yet evidence on asymmetric and dynamic production responses remains limited. This study investigates the short-run and long-run effects of climate variability on crop and livestock production in Somalia using annual data for 1989–2021. item.title: Assessment of heavy metal contamination hotspots in the Ramsar-designated East Kolkata Wetlands
item.description: Environmental Monitoring and Assessment — Abstract Urban wetlands worldwide are increasingly impacted by anthropogenic effluents, leading to heavy metal accumulation with significant ecological and human health implications. This study presents an assessment of heavy metal contamination in the East Kolkata Wetlands (EKW), a Ramsar-designated wetland in India where sediment samples from fifteen sites encompassing industrially influenced and peripheral zones were analysed for heavy metals including Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Cobalt, Copper, Lead, Manganese, Mercury, Molybdenum, Nickel, Selenium, Vanadium, and Zinc. item.description: Discover Internet of Things — In urban high-density building clusters, fires not only tend to spread rapidly within individual buildings but can also breach building boundaries and propagate to adjacent structures. Traditional field simulation methods suffer from high computational costs and significant response delays, while existing data-driven models struggle to capture long-range dependencies across multiple buildings. item.description: Scientific Data — Abstract MaterialCities is a dataset of the gross floor area and the mass of eight construction materials of the world’s buildings in high resolution and detail. It differentiates floor area and material stocks by three building functions and five load-bearing structural types with region-specific construction archetypes using variant material intensity ranges that capture building materials’ inherent uncertainties and variabilities. item.description: Child Abuse & Neglect — Background Neglect is the most frequently reported but least studied form of child maltreatment. Because it arises in part from the conditions under which care is provided, neglect may be sensitive to environmental stressors associated with a warming climate. item.description: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education — Market liberalization has reshaped agricultural production by transforming farming practices, labour relations, and institutional arrangements that influence smallholder productivity.However, empirical evidence on how these interconnected transformations affect maize production efficiency remains limited, particularly in Kenya.This study examined the influence of changing farming practices and labour relations on maize production efficiency among smallholder farmers in Trans-Nzoia County, Kenya.A convergent mixed-methods design was employed involving 385 randomly selected maize farmers, comple

item.title: How does physical exercise relate to residents’ perceived social fairness? An empirical study based on CGSS 2023 data
item.description: Frontiers in Psychology — Introduction Physical exercise may be associated not only with physical and psychological well-being but also with residents’ evaluations of the broader social environment. However, evidence regarding the relationship between physical exercise and perceived social fairness and its potential explanatory pathways remains limited. This study examined the association between physical exercise and perceived social fairness among Chinese residents and explored the potential roles of social interaction, social support, and social trust. item.description: Frontiers in Environmental Economics — European countries are developing ambitious climate adaptation strategies, yet implementation remains fragmented, underfunded and frequently misaligned with multi-level governance capacities. Developed within the Horizon 2020 IMPETUS project, this study presents a multi-method, co-production-oriented approach that connects the assessment of governance, policy and financing barriers with the development of actionable policy recommendations across seven European regions. item.description: Frontiers in Environmental Science — Introduction Digital twins can support maintenance of environmental monitoring infrastructure, but dependable decisions require consistent treatment of uncertain condition, usable sensing service, and intervention timing. item.description: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media — Research based on the biomedical model, spanning various fields, has addressed physical functional impairment and psychological distress separately, with most previous explanations centered on the individual level. item.description: Discover Education — This study examined the effects of Multiple Intelligences Theory (MIT), re-conceptualized as an instructional design heuristic rather than a validated cognitive model, on argumentative writing skills among English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners at an Ethiopian university. item.description: Frontiers in Political Science — This study examines the relational and interpretive dimensions of policy-network implementation in the Fisheries Cultivation Village Program in XIII Koto Kampar District, Riau Province, Indonesia. item.description: Journal of Anatolian Environmental and Animal Sciences — This study examines the environmental and socio-economic impacts of the 2025 wildfires in Los Angeles County using remote sensing (RS) and geographic information systems (GIS). item.description: Springer eBooks — This chapter examines the complex relationship between migration and food security through a case study of refugees in Kitchener–Waterloo, Canada. item.description: Springer eBooks — The COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa manifested as a syndemic, in which the virus interacted with pre-existing comorbidities and inequalities in food security, employment, and social protection to intensify vulnerability.
